title: A Borrowed CB350 and a Submerged Church
description: A solo birthday ride from Bengaluru to the Shettihalli church near Hassan on a rented Honda CB350: four toll gates, a long string of chai-and-snack stops, one tank of fuel, a drowned church and a village offroad.

stops.name: S.G. Palya, Bengaluru
stops.label: Home · 05:30
stops.note: Tank full, nobody awake. Rolled out before sunrise.

stops.name: Sri Maruthi Family Restaurant, Kunigal
stops.label: Morning meal
stops.treat: A proper South-Indian breakfast if you rolled out before yours.

stops.name: N R Gowdru Tea Cafe, Hurkehalli
stops.label: Chai stop
stops.treat: A no-fuss highway chai cabin — the first good break out of the city.

stops.name: Kadamba Veg, Bellur Cross
stops.label: Lunch / dinner
stops.treat: The sit-down veg thali, right by the toll gate — ideal on the way back.

stops.name: Hassan
stops.label: Hassan
stops.note: Rolled through Hassan on the way to the church.

stops.name: Shettihalli Rosary Church
stops.label: The church
stops.note: The reason for all of it — the Gothic ruin that drowns and resurfaces every year.

stops.name: Shettihalli Bridge
stops.label: The bridge
stops.note: Out onto the bridge over the Hemavati backwaters for the full view of the ruin.

stops.name: Masti Gudi, Ganjigere
stops.label: Village offroad
stops.note: Dropped off the tarmac and picked my way around the village to the little Masti Gudi shrine.

stops.name: Home — S.G. Palya
stops.label: Home · dusk
stops.note: Same NH75 back east, through Nagasandra and Majestic. 600 km, one drowned church, ₹1,400 lighter, and not even slightly sorry.

gallery.cap: On the highway — the open road out of the city.
The rented CB350, before rolling out.
Green fields on the way west.
The ruin across the sand, the water pulled back.
The Gothic facade, still standing after 160 years.
Inside the nave, sky where the roof should be.
The tower and the old doorway.
The CB350 out on the backwater sand.
The Hemavati backwaters that drown it every year.
